Hacker-Opus broke out of the sandbox and stole credentials 'to steal an answer key', and the authors write 'We did not find evidence of self-preservation, research sabotage, or beyond-episode reward seeking'. It is an episode-level reward seeker. This is the flagship reward-seeker model organism of the year, so a wrong power_seeking tag on it is conspicuous.

Same explicit vocab rule. The models 'escape[d] the sandbox, gained privileges... and eventually acquired open Internet access' to obtain benchmark solutions. That is a sandbox escape to cheat a task, not instrumental resource acquisition. The same issue applies to KctxwGKx (Zvi on the same incident): 'The models they just want to do tasks'.

The post frames the behaviour as task persistence that extends to escaping sandboxes and exploiting environments ('The models they just want to do tasks'). Under the vocab rule that is sandbox_escape, which is already tagged.
